mappings.note: Part (a) an animal that changes sex is a heredity mechanism that is expressly not chromosomal, so C 3.3 and not C 3.3-LO-3, which is restricted to human beings; part (b) fossils are evidence, so C 4.5.

Three terms, three different outcomes: the trait that expresses itself in the next generation is dominance (LO-2), the trait an organism has by inheritance is C 3.3-LO-2, and the origin of a new species is C 4.5-LO-1. Dropping any code would leave a part of the item unmapped.
Meaning of recessive and dominant genes: LO-2 is the only outcome that distinguishes them. No cross is worked, so not LO-1.
Fossils, their formation and their significance: evidence of evolution, which no learning outcome reaches.
Parts (a) and (b) are heredity and which traits can be passed on, i.e. the germ-line gene argument (LO-2); part (c) is the wild-cabbage artificial-selection illustration, which is evidence (C 4.5).
Parts (a) Darwin and (c) ordering organisms by evolution are evidence-side (C 4.5); part (b) what Mendel concluded about traits is the dominant-or-recessive conclusion (LO-2).
Tracing evolutionary relationships through homologous organs: evidence.

Part (a) homologous or analogous is evidence (C 4.5); part (b) define variation is the competency about variation as change in DNA sequence, and not C 4.5-LO-1, because a bare definition says nothing about accumulation.
Make a cross and give the F2 genotypes and the white-to-purple ratio is LO-1; the item supplies an OBSERVED count (75 of 100 white) to be checked against the 3:1 prediction, which is C 8.2-LO-3.
Part (a) geographical isolation is mechanism and part (b) homologous or analogous is evidence; the shared competency is cited rather than LO-1 alongside its own parent.
Why 46 plus 46 chromosomes does not give 46 pairs is answered by gametes carrying one chromosome of each pair: genes carried on chromosomes, LO-2.
What evolution of species means plus two evidences for it: the item is explicitly about evidence, which no learning outcome covers.
Boy-or-girl as a matter of chance, justified with an illustration, is human sex determination.
Teeth and elephant tusks as homologous, and what analogous organs indicate: evidence on both halves.
Green beetles increasing in a green bush is natural selection on existing variation, and the advantages of variation follow from it. Mechanism, not evidence.
Part (a) defining inherited traits is C 3.3-LO-2; part (b) inherited traits directing evolution is the accumulation argument, C 4.5-LO-1.
Homologous structures in vertebrates and how they help establish evolutionary relationship: evidence.
Define a fossil, identify an invertebrate fossil and say what evidence it provides: evidence throughout. The diagram did not survive extraction, but the outcome is unaffected.
RR crossed with rr, phenotype and genotype of F1 and F2: a monohybrid cross whose ratios must be predicted.
Genetic drift, natural selection and reproductive isolation are the three mechanisms by which variation is fixed and species split; all mechanism, none evidence.
A 9:3:3:1 F2 ratio is the dihybrid cross, and the item asks which rule it demonstrates: LO-1 predicts the ratios obtained.
Pure tall crossed with pure dwarf, F1 selfed to F2, is a monohybrid cross. The sub-questions did not survive extraction, but the cross named in the stem fixes the outcome.
Acquired versus inherited traits in tabular form: the germ-line gene argument.
Sex of a new born as a matter of chance, with a flow chart: human sex determination.
Cousin marriage is discouraged because two carriers can bring a hidden recessive factor together, which is LO-2. Not C 4.4-LO-1: no ratio has to be computed.
That the F2 dominants are not all the same is the genotype-versus-phenotype point (TT against Tt behind one appearance), which is exactly LO-2, and not the 3:1 ratio itself.
Round-green crossed with wrinkled-yellow, F1 genotype and the F2 types with their ratios: a dihybrid cross worked for ratios.
Round crossed with wrinkled, with observations and reasons for F1 and F2: a monohybrid cross and its ratio. The contrasting-characters list in part (b) is incidental.
A trait may be inherited but not expressed is the recessive-carrier point, which LO-2 names; no ratio is wanted.

Which type of organs are shown and what origin and structure they have is the homologous-or-analogous call, i.e. evidence. The figure did not survive extraction, but either answer lands on the same competency.
Whether a bird wing appeared in stages or at one stroke is the accumulation-of-variation argument, LO-1, not an evidence question.
Part (a) gene flow preventing speciation is mechanism, part (b) which fossils retain fine detail is evidence; the shared competency is cited rather than LO-1 alongside its own parent.
Homologous organs, analogous organs and fossils as evidence in favour of evolution: three evidence categories, no learning outcome.
Speciation and natural selection are both mechanism, so LO-1 and not the evidence-side competency.
The approximate F2 ratio and the law it belongs to is LO-1 applying Mendel laws and predicting ratios. The cross it refers to sat in a figure that did not survive extraction.

Part (a) the two characteristics deciding analogy and homology is evidence. Part (b), the basis for classifying organisms as prokaryote or eukaryote, reaches no code in this frame and no second code is invented for it.
Who Mendel was and what he contributed to heredity uses no specific cross, ratio or dominance call, so it sits at the competency naming Mendel laws rather than at either outcome.
Kohlrabi, cauliflower, broccoli and cabbage and how long cabbage has been cultivated is the artificial-selection illustration: evidence.
Formation of a beetle sub-population is variation accumulating in a part of a population: mechanism.
At what stage sex is determined (at fertilisation, by the sperm) is human sex determination.
What happens if both F1 characters pass together into F2 is the independent-assortment question, answered through the dihybrid cross and its ratio.
Why offspring resemble parents more than grandparents is answered by which genes on which chromosomes were actually passed on: LO-2.
Attached ear lobes against body weight is the inherited-versus-acquired call, which rests on the germ-line genes.

MISFILED: the aquarium care item is an ecosystem and values question with no heredity or evolution content. No competency in this frame is true; interconnectedness between organisms and their environment is the only honest statement.
Part (a) males are heterogametic is human sex determination (LO-3); part (b) inherited against acquired characters is the germ-line gene argument (LO-2).
What happened to the dwarf trait in F1 and why it reappears in F2 is the recessive-is-hidden-not-lost point, which LO-2 names. The ratio itself is not asked for, so not LO-1.
Whether the monohybrid TT x tt result generalises to a law is applying Mendel laws to a monohybrid cross and reading its F2. Not LO-2: the question is about the law, not about naming the dominant.
Tabulating dominant against recessive is LO-2; computing the proportion of round seeds in F2 is LO-1. The item explicitly demands both.
Three factors providing evidence in favour of evolution: evidence, which no learning outcome in this frame reaches.
Mendel experiment on one visible contrasting character is the monohybrid cross with its F1 and F2 ratios.
Evolution and classification being interlinked is an argument from shared characteristics, i.e. evidence.
The item ends on what genes are and where they are located, which is LO-2 word for word; the Mendel-factors part is the same statement in historical dress.
Part (iii), the mechanism of human sex determination, is LO-3; parts (i) and (ii) ask what chromosomes are and where they are seated, which is LO-2.
Geographical isolation and the formation of a species from very different but interbreeding individuals: speciation mechanism.
Five vegetables from one wild ancestor by artificial selection, with the feature selected for in each: the artificial-selection evidence illustration.
Defining evolution and listing four ways a trait increases in a population are both mechanism: selection, drift, gene flow, mutation.
Parts (i) and (ii), traits and the inherited-against-acquired split, are C 3.3-LO-2; part (iii) speciation and its factors is C 4.5-LO-1.
Part (a) acquired against inherited traits is C 3.3-LO-2; part (b) speciation and its factors is C 4.5-LO-1.
Fossils, their formation and how they support evolution: evidence.

Five terms across three outcomes: gene is C 3.3-LO-2, genetic drift and evolution are C 4.5-LO-1, recessive trait is C 4.4-LO-2. Genetics itself falls under the first. All three are needed to cover the item.
Part (a) somatic against germinal variation is the germ-line mechanism (C 3.3-LO-2); part (b) two ways a trait increases in a population is C 4.5-LO-1.
Part (a) traits may be dominant or recessive is LO-2; part (b) traits are inherited independently is the dihybrid cross, LO-1. The item is built from exactly these two halves.
Fossils, their formation, two dating methods and their role in the study of evolution: evidence throughout.
Three contrasts on three different outcomes: heredity against variation is C 3.3, dominant against recessive is C 4.4-LO-2, natural against artificial selection is C 4.5. None subsumes another.
Parts (a) and (b), homozygous breeding true and heterozygous, are the genotype-against-phenotype distinction (LO-2); part (c) speciation is C 4.5-LO-1.

Mendel yellow-round against green-wrinkled schematic is the dihybrid cross and its 9:3:3:1 outcome. The stem is a diagram caption whose sub-questions did not survive extraction; the cross named still fixes the outcome.
Chromosome pairs, which of them are sex chromosomes, and a flow chart for the sex of a new born: human sex determination.

Both halves are about doing science: observing classmates ear lobes and drawing a conclusion from the data, and why Mendel chose pea as experimental material. Not C 8.2-LO-3, since no Punnett square is used; not C 3.3, since the demand is the investigation rather than the biology.
Evolution occurring in stages, and eye against eyespot, are both read off comparative evidence.

Part (a) acquired traits not inherited is C 3.3-LO-2; part (c) variations accumulating and not disappearing is C 4.5-LO-1. Part (b), all humans as one species, sits at the same evolution competency and gets no separate code, since citing C 4.5 alongside its own child adds nothing.
Speciation, four factors, and which cannot apply to a self-pollinating species: mechanism throughout.
Parts (a) and (b), why garden pea and which contrasting characters, are experimental-design choices (C 8.2); part (c), how Mendel interpreted his results as dominant or recessive, is C 4.4-LO-2.
Defining evolution, how it occurs and fossil evidence span mechanism and evidence, so the shared competency is cited rather than LO-1 alongside its own parent.
Human teeth and elephant tusks as homologous organs: evidence of common ancestry.
Which structure is not vestigial: vestigial organs are an evidence category, reached by no learning outcome.
Wild cabbage as an example of artificial selection: the evidence illustration, not a statement about variation accumulating.
Where the earliest human ancestors lived is fossil and molecular evidence about human evolution.
RRyy crossed with rrYY and the resulting F1 seeds is a dihybrid cross whose outcome must be predicted.
Which of carrot, potato, radish and tomato are homologous structures: plant homology, an evidence question.
A trait being influenced by DNA from both parents is the genes-carried-on-chromosomes mechanism, not a cross.
The group sharing the most characters in common is the classification-as-evidence-of-descent argument.
What generally causes a new species to form: speciation mechanism, not evidence.
Feathered dinosaurs that could not fly is fossil evidence that a structure can be adapted to a new function.
Naming artificial selection as the process of human-directed selection: the evidence illustration.
Identifying a homologous pair: evidence of common ancestry.
Why TT x tt gives all tall progeny is the dominance relation, LO-2. The 1:1 make-up of F1 is not the demand, so not LO-1.
The number of sex-chromosome pairs in a human zygote is part of human sex determination.
Asks what the child blood group will be, i.e. predicts the progeny of a given cross (LO-1). Contrast qid 86418, which asks which allele is dominant and is therefore LO-2.
Progeny of tall-round crossed with short-wrinkled: a dihybrid cross whose outcome must be predicted.
Same dihybrid RRyy x rrYY prediction as qid 104893, of which this is a near-verbatim duplicate.
Genetic roots of the human species: molecular and fossil evidence of human evolution.
Wild cabbage as the ancestor of broccoli: the artificial-selection evidence illustration.
The described process, where helpful characteristics are passed on and unhelpful ones are not, is natural selection: mechanism, not evidence.
Extinct organisms known only from fossils: fossil evidence.
What decides the sex of the child: human sex determination.
A trait absent in F1 that reappears in F2 identifies which parent is recessive: the dominance call, LO-2, not the 3:1 ratio.
A 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio identifies a dihybrid cross: LO-1 predicts the ratios obtained.
Which characters can be acquired but not inherited is the germ-line gene argument.
Same basic structure with different functions defines homologous organs: evidence.
Different basic structure with similar function defines analogous organs: evidence.
Remains and impressions of organisms from the remote past are fossils: evidence.
The process by which new species arise is speciation: mechanism, not evidence.
Which example counts as genetic variation is about variation as a change in DNA sequence, the competency. Not C 4.5-LO-1: nothing about accumulation over generations is asked.
Recognising continuous variation is again about the nature of variation itself, not about its accumulation or its Mendelian inheritance.
The more characters two species share, the closer their relationship: classification as evidence of descent.
Genetic drift against natural selection is a contrast between two mechanisms that change allele frequency: LO-1, not evidence.
Which idea was absent from Darwin theory is a question about the mechanism of natural selection, not about the evidence for evolution.
What survival of the fittest actually describes is the natural-selection mechanism acting on variation.
How human offspring sex is determined: LO-3.
Wild cabbage giving rise to cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower by artificial selection: the evidence illustration.
Archaeopteryx as a connecting link is fossil evidence of common ancestry.
Feathered dinosaurs as fossil evidence that a structure can be adapted to a new function. Verbatim duplicate of qid 104898.
Identifying an impossible outcome of a pure tall by pure short cross requires predicting the legitimate F1 and F2 ratios: LO-1.

Which statement is not a direct conclusion from Mendel work is about the standing of the laws themselves rather than about any particular cross or ratio, so it sits at the competency and not at LO-1 or LO-2.
A possible F2 progeny from tall-round by short-wrinkled is a dihybrid ratio prediction.
A section of DNA providing information for one protein is a gene, which is the LO-2 mechanism.
Which of weight and height is gene-controlled is the inherited-against-acquired call resting on genes carried on chromosomes.
